mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists four topics where the Torah tells us two kinds, and the Sages learn that there are really four: oaths, tumah in the Beis HaMikdash, carrying on Shabbos, and tzaraas marks.

chunks.en: Oaths: there are two kinds that are really four.
chunks.st: With regard to oaths on an utterance of the lips, there are two types that are actually four types.
chunks.stMore: The Torah specifies only two types of oaths whose violation renders one liable to bring a sliding-scale offering to atone for his transgression (see Leviticus 5:4): Where a person takes an oath to perform some action, and where he takes an oath to refrain from performing some action. With regard to both types, the Torah explicitly mentions liability only for an oath pertaining to one’s future behavior. Nevertheless, the Sages derive that one is also liable for a violation of both types of oaths when they pertain to one’s past behavior. Accordingly, although only two types are explicitly mentioned in the Torah, the Sages derive that there are actually four types. The mishna lists similar groups of halakhot.

words.note: A shevuah is a strong promise, like "I swear I will eat" or "I swear I did not eat."

chunks.en: Knowing about tumah: two kinds that are really four.
chunks.explain: Going into the Beis HaMikdash or eating korbanos while tamei, without remembering.
chunks.st: With regard to cases of awareness of the defiling of the Temple by entering it while one is ritually impure, or defiling its sacrificial foods by partaking of them while one is ritually impure, there are two types that are actually four.
chunks.stMore: It is prohibited for an impure person to enter the Temple (see Numbers 19:20) or to partake of its sacrificial foods (see Leviticus 7:19–20). If one transgressed either prohibition during a lapse of awareness, then upon becoming aware of his transgression, he is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering (see Leviticus 5:2). The Torah specifies that one is liable to bring the offering only in the case in which he had a lapse of awareness of the fact that he was impure. The Sages derive that one is liable not only in these two cases, but also where he was aware of his personal status but had a lapse of awareness concerning the identity of the place he was entering or the status of the foods he ate.

chunks.en: Carrying out on Shabbos: two kinds that are really four.
chunks.st: With regard to acts of carrying out that are prohibited on Shabbat, there are two types that are actually four.
chunks.stMore: On Shabbat, it is prohibited to transfer an item from domain to domain. The Torah explicitly refers to only two cases, both of which involve an item being transferred from a private domain to a public domain: Where the transfer is made by a person who remains in the public domain, and where the transfer is made by a person who remains in the private domain. The Sages derive that liability is incurred in these cases also if the item is transferred from the public domain to the private domain. Although only two types are mentioned by the Torah, the Sages derive that there are actually four types.

chunks.en: The colors of tzaraas marks: two kinds that are really four.
chunks.st: With regard to shades of leprous marks on a person’s skin, there are two types that are actually four.
chunks.stMore: The Torah specifies that if a leprous mark appears on a person’s skin, the afflicted person must undergo a process of purification and then bring various offerings. Part of the classification of these types of leprosy is based on their shade of white. Two types of marks are explicitly mentioned in the Torah, and the Sages derive that each of these two types has a secondary mark.

words.note: Tzaraas is a skin sickness in the Torah; its marks are different shades of white.

chunks.st: As for the boundaries of the Temple with regard to the halakhot of impurity, the same halakha applies to one who enters the area that was part of the original Temple courtyard and

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: or into an added part of the Azarah.
chunks.st: to one who enters the later addition to the Temple courtyard,
chunks.stMore: because the additional section is sanctified with the full sanctity of the Temple courtyard. The mishna notes:

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הָעִיר וְעַל הָעֲזָרוֹת
chunks.en: For we may add to the city of Yerushalayim or to the Azarah
chunks.st: As, additions can be made to the city of Jerusalem or to the Temple courtyards

chunks.he: אֶלָּא בְמֶלֶךְ וְנָבִיא וְאוּרִים וְתֻמִּים וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין
chunks.en: only with a king, a navi, the Urim V'Tumim, and a Sanhedrin
chunks.st: only by a special body comprising the king, a prophet, the Urim VeTummim, and the Sanhedrin

words.note: The Urim V'Tumim were in the Kohen Gadol's choshen; through them Hashem gave answers.

chunks.he: שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד וּבִשְׁתֵּי תוֹדוֹת וּבְשִׁיר.
chunks.en: of seventy-one judges, and with two korbanos todah, and with song.
chunks.st: of seventy-one judges, and with two thanks-offerings and with a special song.
chunks.stMore: Once the addition to the courtyard is made by this body and this process, it is given the full sanctity of the original courtyard area. The mishna provides certain details of the consecration ceremony.

words.note: A todah is a thank-you korban that comes with loaves of bread.

chunks.he: וּבֵית דִּין מְהַלְּכִין וּשְׁתֵּי תוֹדוֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: The beis din walk forward, with the two todahs behind them,
chunks.st: And the court would move forward, and two thanks-offerings would be brought after them,

chunks.en: and all of Yisrael behind them.
chunks.st: and all of the Jewish people would follow behind them.

chunks.en: The inner todah is eaten, and the outer one is burned.
chunks.st: When they would reach the end of the place that they desired to consecrate, the inner thanks-offering would be eaten and the outer one would be burned. The details of this ceremony will be described in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And any part that was not added with all of these,
chunks.st: And with regard to any addition to the Temple that was not made with all these ceremonial procedures,

chunks.en: one who goes in there while tamei is not chayav for it.
chunks.st: one who enters there while ritually impure is not liable
chunks.stMore: to bring an offering if his entry was unwitting, nor to be punished with karet, excision from the World-to-Come, if his entry was intentional.

words.note: Chayav: he must bring a korban or get a punishment.

mishnayos.summary: If a person became tamei inside the Azarah and forgot, and then bowed down, or stayed there, or went out the long way, he is chayav. If he went out the short way, he is patur.

chunks.en: If he became tamei in the Azarah and forgot
chunks.st: The mishna proceeds to consider a case involving one who was ritually pure when he entered the Temple but who became impure while in the Temple courtyard, and afterward, his impurity was hidden from him

chunks.en: that he was tamei, but remembered it was the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: but he remembered that he was standing in the Temple,

chunks.en: or he forgot it was the Beis HaMikdash, but remembered he was tamei,
chunks.st: or the fact that he was standing in the Temple was hidden from him but he remembered his impurity,

chunks.en: or he forgot both this and that,
chunks.st: or both this fact and that fact were hidden from him. In all these cases,

chunks.en: and he bowed down, or stayed there as long as it takes to bow down,
chunks.st: if he bowed down, or he tarried in the Temple courtyard long enough to bow down even though he did not actually bow,

chunks.en: or he went out the long way,
chunks.st: or he went out by way of a longer route when he could have taken a shorter route,

chunks.en: he is chayav. If he went out the short way,
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering. But if he left the Temple via the shortest way,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. זוֹ הִיא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: he is patur. This is the "mitzvah to do" about the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: he is exempt. This mitzva that the ritually impure must be sent out of the Temple is the positive mitzva concerning the Temple for which, as is taught elsewhere in the Mishna (Horayot 8b),

words.note: He does not have to bring a korban.

words.en: that is in the Beis HaMikdash

chunks.en: that beis din is not chayav a korban for.
chunks.explain: If beis din ruled wrongly about it, they do not bring a korban.
chunks.st: the Sanhedrin is not liable to bring an offering for an erroneous ruling.
chunks.stMore: A communal bull sin-offering is brought because of the unwitting transgression of a prohibition involving an action by the Jewish people resulting from an erroneous halakhic decision handed down by the Sanhedrin. But if the Sanhedrin mistakenly ruled that one who became impure while in the Temple may leave by way of a longer route, they do not bring this offering, as it is brought only for an erroneous ruling on a matter that requires the bringing of a fixed sin-offering, and not a sliding-scale offering, for its unwitting violation.

mishnayos.stIntro: The first part of the mishna discussed one who became ritually impure before entering the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah gives an example of a "mitzvah to do" about a niddah: a husband must move away from his wife in the right way when she becomes tamei.

chunks.en: And which "mitzvah to do"
about a niddah makes beis din chayav a korban?

words.note: A woman during the time she is tamei, when she and her husband must stay apart.

chunks.en: If a man was with his wife when she was tahor,
and she told him, "I have become tamei,"
and he moved away from her right away,

chunks.he: חַיָּב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיְּצִיאָתוֹ הֲנָאָה לוֹ כְּבִיאָתוֹ:
chunks.en: he is chayav, because the way he left counts just like staying.

mishnayos.summary: Which forgetting makes a person bring the korban? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva say only forgetting that he was tamei, not forgetting that it was the Beis HaMikdash. Rabbi Yishmael says both.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: With regard to the sliding-scale offering the verse states:

chunks.en: The pasuk says, "a sheretz... and it was hidden from him":
chunks.st: “Or if a person touches any impure thing, whether it is the carcass of a non-kosher undomesticated animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher domesticated animal, or the carcass of a non-kosher creeping animal, and it is hidden from him” (Leviticus 5:2).

words.note: A sheretz is one of eight small creatures whose dead body makes a person tamei.

chunks.en: he is chayav for forgetting the sheretz,
chunks.explain: That is, forgetting that he became tamei.
chunks.st: A precise reading of this verse indicates that in a case where one has a lapse of awareness that he had contracted ritual impurity by touching a creeping animal, he is liable
chunks.stMore: to bring a sliding-scale offering for having defiled the Temple or the sacrificial food,

chunks.en: but he is not chayav for forgetting the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: but he is not liable to bring such an offering in a case where he has a lapse of awareness that he is entering the Temple or partaking of sacrificial food.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Similarly, Rabbi Akiva says: The verse states:

chunks.en: The pasuk says, "and it was hidden from him, and he is tamei":
chunks.st: “And it is hidden from him, so that he is impure” (Leviticus 5:2),

chunks.en: he is chayav for forgetting tumah,
chunks.st: thereby teaching that in a case when one has a lapse of awareness that he had contracted ritual impurity, he is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering,

chunks.en: but he is not chayav for forgetting the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: but one is not liable to bring such an offering in a case when he has a lapse of awareness that he is entering the Temple or partaking of sacrificial food.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says: The verse states:

chunks.en: "And it was hidden" is written two times,
chunks.st: “And it is hidden from him” (Leviticus 5:2), and it states: “And it is hidden from him” (Leviticus 5:3), twice,

chunks.en: to make him chayav for forgetting tumah
chunks.st: in order to render one liable to bring a sliding-scale offering both in a case where one has a lapse of awareness that he had contracted ritual impurity

chunks.en: and for forgetting the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and in a case where one has a lapse of awareness that he is entering the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: Oaths about eating: what counts as breaking an oath not to eat, and when a person must bring one korban or two.

chunks.en: Oaths: there are two kinds that are really four.
chunks.st: With regard to oaths attesting to the truth about an utterance, which, when violated, render one liable to bring a sliding-scale offering, there are two types that are actually four types.
chunks.stMore: The initial two oaths, which relate to utterances about the future and are explicitly prohibited in the Torah, are:

chunks.en: "I swear I will eat," or "I swear I will not eat."
chunks.st: On my oath I will eat, or: On my oath I will not eat.
chunks.stMore: These are expanded to four, to include oaths concerning utterances about the past:

chunks.en: "I swear I ate," or "I swear I did not eat."
chunks.st: On my oath I ate, or: On my oath I did not eat. If one says:

chunks.he: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אֹכַל וְאָכַל כָּל שֶׁהוּא,
chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat," and he ate even a tiny bit,
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat, and he then ate any amount, even less than an olive-bulk,

chunks.en: he is chayav. These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: he is liable; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: The Sages said to Rabbi Akiva,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: Where do we find that one who eats any tiny amount
chunks.st: Where do we find that one who eats any

chunks.en: is chayav,
chunks.st: amount is liable, leading you to say

chunks.en: that this person should be chayav?
chunks.st: that this person is liable?

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to them:

chunks.he: וְכִי הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ בִּמְדַבֵּר וּמֵבִיא קָרְבָּן,
chunks.en: And where do we find one who just speaks and brings a korban,
chunks.st: And where do we find one who speaks and is liable to bring an offering for it,

chunks.en: the way this person just speaks and brings a korban?
chunks.explain: Here he brings a korban just for words, so a tiny bit of food is also enough.
chunks.st: as this oath taker merely speaks, i.e., takes an oath, and brings an offering for it?
chunks.stMore: If one said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat," and he ate and drank,
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat, and then he ate and drank,

chunks.en: he brings only one korban.
chunks.explain: Not eating includes not drinking.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one
chunks.stMore: offering, because an oath to refrain from eating includes refraining from drinking. If he said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat and I will not
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat and I will not

chunks.en: drink," and he ate and drank,
chunks.st: drink, and then he ate and drank,

chunks.en: he brings two korbanos.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring two offerings.

mishnayos.summary: If he swore not to eat, and then ate many kinds of bread, he brings one korban. If he named each kind of bread in his oath, he brings a korban for each one.

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat,"
chunks.st: If he said: On my oath I will not eat, and

chunks.en: and he ate wheat bread, and
chunks.st: then he ate wheat bread and

chunks.en: barley bread, and spelt bread,
chunks.st: barley bread and spelt bread,

chunks.en: he brings only one korban.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one offering.
chunks.stMore: If he said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat wheat bread,
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat wheat bread

chunks.en: or barley bread, or spelt bread,"
chunks.st: or barley bread or spelt bread,

chunks.he: וְאָכַל, חַיָּב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת:
chunks.en: and he ate them, he is chayav for each and every one.
chunks.st: and then he ate all of them, he is liable to bring an offering for each and every one.

mishnayos.summary: The same is true for drinks: one oath not to drink brings one korban, but if he named each drink, he brings a korban for each.

chunks.he: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אֶשְׁתֶּה וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִין הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not drink," and he drank many drinks,
chunks.st: If he said: On my oath I will not drink, and then he drank several kinds of liquids,

chunks.en: he brings only one korban.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one offering.
chunks.stMore: If he said:

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not drink wine,
chunks.st: On my oath I will not drink wine

chunks.en: or oil, or honey," and he drank them,
chunks.st: or oil or honey, and then he drank all of them,

chunks.en: he is chayav for each and every one.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring an offering for each and every one.

mishnayos.summary: An oath not to eat does not include things that are not food. Does it include non-kosher food? The Sages say yes; Rabbi Shimon says no. With a konam on his wife, everyone agrees it counts.

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat,"
chunks.st: If he said: On my oath I will not eat,

chunks.en: and he ate things that are not fit to eat,
chunks.st: and he ate foods that are inedible

chunks.en: or drank things that are not fit to drink,
chunks.st: or drank liquids that are not potable,

chunks.en: he is patur. If he said, "I swear I will not eat,"
chunks.st: he is exempt. If he said: On my oath I will not eat,

chunks.en: and he ate neveilos and treifos, sheratzim and creeping creatures,
chunks.explain: Non-kosher things the Torah already forbids.
chunks.st: and then he ate the meat of unslaughtered carcasses or tereifot, repugnant creatures or creeping animals,

words.note: Meat of an animal that died without shechitah.
Meat of an animal with a deadly injury or sickness.

chunks.en: he is chayav. Rabbi Shimon says he is patur.
chunks.explain: Because he is already sworn from Har Sinai not to eat them.
chunks.st: he is liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems him exempt,
chunks.stMore: since he is already under oath from Mount Sinai not to eat them and an oath cannot take effect where another oath is in force.

chunks.en: If he said, "Konam! My wife may not benefit from me
chunks.st: But if he said: It is konam for my wife to derive benefit from me

words.note: A word that makes something forbidden, like a korban.

chunks.en: if I ate today,"
chunks.st: if I ate today,

chunks.he: וְהוּא אָכַל נְבֵלוֹת וּטְרֵפוֹת שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים,
chunks.en: and he had eaten neveilos and treifos, sheratzim and creeping creatures,
chunks.st: and he had eaten carcasses or tereifot, repugnant creatures or creeping animals,

chunks.en: then his wife may not benefit from him.
chunks.st: his wife is prohibited from deriving benefit from him.

mishnayos.summary: An oath counts whether it is about himself or others, about something that matters or something that does not. Rabbi Yishmael says only oaths about the future count; Rabbi Akiva says oaths about the past count too.

chunks.en: It is the same for things about himself,
chunks.st: If one unwittingly takes a false oath about the past or breaks an oath he made about the future, both if it is an oath that addresses matters that concern oneself and

chunks.en: and things about other people,
chunks.st: if it is an oath that addresses matters that concern others,
chunks.stMore: he is liable to bring a sliding-scale offering for an oath on an utterance.

chunks.en: and things that make a difference,
chunks.st: And likewise, an oath on an utterance may address both tangible matters

chunks.en: and things that make no difference.
chunks.explain: Like throwing a pebble into the sea.
chunks.st: and intangible matters.

chunks.en: How so? If he said,
chunks.st: How so? Examples of oaths about future actions that concern others are if one said:

chunks.he: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֶתֵּן לְאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי וְשֶׁלֹּא אֶתֵּן,
chunks.en: "I swear I will give something to so-and-so," or "that I will not give,"
chunks.st: On my oath I will give so-and-so a particular item, or: On my oath I will not give it to him.
chunks.stMore: Examples of such oaths about the past are if one said:

chunks.en: "that I gave," or "that I did not give,"
chunks.st: On my oath I gave another a particular item, or: On my oath I did not give it to him.
chunks.stMore: Examples of oaths about the future that address intangible matters are where one said:

chunks.en: "that I will sleep," or "that I will not sleep,"
chunks.st: On my oath I will sleep, or: On my oath I will not sleep. Examples of such oaths about the past are where one said:

chunks.en: "that I slept," or "that I did not sleep,"
chunks.st: On my oath I slept, or: On my oath I did not sleep.
chunks.stMore: Other examples of oaths about intangible matters are when one takes an oath, saying:

chunks.en: "that I will throw a pebble into the sea," or "that I will not throw,"
chunks.st: I will throw a stone into the sea, or: I will not throw it, or:

chunks.en: "that I threw," or "that I did not throw."
chunks.st: I threw it, or: I did not throw it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,
chunks.en: One is chayav only for an oath about the future,
chunks.st: One is liable only for an oath on an utterance taken about the future,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "to do bad or to do good."
chunks.explain: These words talk about things he will do later.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Or if anyone take an oath clearly with his lips to do evil, or to do good,
chunks.stMore: whatsoever it be that a man shall utter clearly with an oath” (Leviticus 5:4). The Torah refers explicitly only to oaths about what one will do in the future.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: If so, I only know about
chunks.st: If so, and one is liable only for oaths explicitly mentioned in the verse, then I have derived only that one is liable for an oath on an utterance with regard to

chunks.en: things where there is doing bad or doing good.
chunks.st: matters to which doing evil and doing good apply.

chunks.he: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן הֲרָעָה וַהֲטָבָה מִנַּיִן.
chunks.en: From where do we learn things where there is no doing bad or good?
chunks.st: From where do I derive that one is liable for an oath on an utterance with regard to matters to which doing evil and doing good do not apply?

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said to him: The halakha in these cases is derived

chunks.en: From the extra words in the pasuk.
chunks.st: by amplification of the meaning of the verse.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: If the pasuk adds for this,
chunks.st: If the verse is amplified for this,
chunks.stMore: i.e., to extend the halakha of an oath on an utterance to matters that do not involve doing evil or good,

chunks.en: then the pasuk adds for that too.
chunks.explain: Then oaths about the past count too.
chunks.st: the verse is amplified for that, i.e., oaths about the past.

mishnayos.summary: If someone swears not to do a mitzvah, or to do a mitzvah, and breaks the oath, he does not bring a korban. Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira argued that he should be chayav, and the Sages answered him.

chunks.he: נִשְׁבַּע לְבַטֵּל אֶת הַמִּצְוָה וְלֹא בִטֵּל,
chunks.en: If he swore not to do a mitzvah, and he did it anyway,
chunks.st: If one takes an oath to refrain from performing a mitzva and he does not refrain,

chunks.en: he is patur. If he swore to do it, and did not do it,
chunks.st: he is exempt from bringing an offering for an oath on an utterance. If he takes an oath to perform a mitzva and he does not perform it,

chunks.en: he is patur, even though it would make sense
chunks.st: he is also exempt, though it would have been fitting

chunks.en: that he should be chayav,
chunks.st: to claim that he is liable to bring the offering,

chunks.en: as Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says.
chunks.st: in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira. The mishna explains:

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira said:

chunks.en: If for an optional thing, which he is not
chunks.st: What? If, with regard to an oath concerning an optional matter, for which one is not

words.note: Something a person may choose to do or not, like eating.

chunks.en: sworn about from Har Sinai,
chunks.st: under oath from Mount Sinai,

chunks.en: he is chayav for it,
chunks.st: he is liable for breaking it, then with regard to an oath about

chunks.he: מִצְוָה שֶׁהוּא מֻשְׁבָּע עָלֶיהָ מֵהַר סִינַי,
chunks.en: then for a mitzvah, which he is sworn about from Har Sinai,
chunks.st: a mitzva, for which he is under oath from Mount Sinai,

chunks.en: isn't it logical that he should be chayav for it?
chunks.st: is it not logical that he would be liable for breaking it?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: No! You can say that about an oath on an optional thing,
chunks.st: No, if you said that one is liable for breaking an oath concerning an optional action,

chunks.en: because there the Torah made "not doing" the same as "doing."
chunks.explain: An oath not to do it counts just like an oath to do it.
chunks.st: where the Torah rendered one liable for a negative oath not to perform it like for a positive oath to perform it,

chunks.en: But can you say that about an oath on a mitzvah, where
chunks.st: shall you also say one is liable with regard to breaking an oath concerning a mitzva, where

chunks.en: the Torah did not make "not doing" the same as "doing"?
chunks.st: the Torah did not render one liable for a negative oath like for a positive oath,

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם נִשְׁבַּע לְבַטֵּל וְלֹא בִטֵּל, פָּטוּר:
chunks.en: For if he swore not to do a mitzvah and did it, he is patur.
chunks.st: since if one takes an oath to refrain from performing a mitzva and did not refrain, he is exempt.

mishnayos.summary: If he swore three times not to eat the same loaf and then ate it, he is chayav only once. Breaking a shevuas bitui on purpose brings malkos, and by mistake a korban. A shevuas shav on purpose brings malkos, and by mistake nothing.

chunks.en: If he said, "I swear I will not eat this loaf,"
chunks.st: If one says: On my oath I will not eat this loaf, and he then says again:

chunks.en: "I swear I will not eat it,"
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat it, and again:

chunks.en: "I swear I will not eat it,"
chunks.st: On my oath I will not eat it, and he

chunks.en: and then he ate it, he is chayav only once.
